PRODUCT REFERENCE: Product fidelity takes priority. Preserve its exact shape, proportions, design, colour, pattern, fabric/material appearance, stitching, silhouette, existing logos, label text and accessories actually supplied. CREATIVE DIRECTION:

Product identity comes first: if a product reference is attached, preserve its exact shape, proportions, design, colour, fabric or material appearance, pattern, stitching, existing logos, label text and supplied accessories. The presentation below must not replace or redesign the supplied product. Do not erase branding or invent lettering. Create an eight-second reel of the supplied skincare bottle standing on pale travertine beside a single olive leaf, realistic glass thickness and clean controlled reflections.

Appearance: Only when no product reference is supplied, use this example: one small cylindrical amber glass bottle with rounded shoulders, a short neck, a ribbed black screw cap and a clean rectangular cream label without lettering. Preserve the amber transparency and visible glass base.

Pose and expression: Place the bottle upright and centred on pale porous travertine, with a small olive sprig lying beside its base and a second stone block softly behind it.

Essential visible details: One reference bottle with its actual cap and existing label intact (black cap and blank cream label only for the no-reference example), travertine pores and restrained olive leaves. Show the cap and base completely; keep reflections narrow enough to see the bottle shape.

Camera and framing: 90mm macro lens, f/8, eye-level to slightly raised three-quarter product view with the complete bottle and generous negative space. Compose for a 9:16 image. Keep the entire object inside the crop. Preserve material texture, accurate geometry, refraction and physically plausible contact shadows. No extra objects or distorted labels. Avoid artificial HDR halos, excessive smoothing, watermarks and unwanted text. Prioritize the essential visible details over decorative background elements.

0–2 seconds: Establish the exact styling, people, objects and setting described above. Keep the complete subject visible.

6–8 seconds: Settle into the starting composition and hold through second 8, with natural breathing or ambient motion only. The final hold is included in the eight-second duration.
